# Copy review feedback: home, hydronic overview, how it works

**Reviewer:** Marketing & Growth agent
**Date:** 21 August 2026
**Scope:** `index.html`, `hydronic/index.html`, `hydronic/how-it-works/index.html` and its embedded interactive. Other pages were grepped for contradicting claims but not reviewed.
**Filed here rather than in `.claude/copy-review/`** because that folder is regenerated by `npm run copy:dump` and this is not derived from the HTML.

Findings are `path:line`, current text, proposed replacement. Nothing was edited and nothing deployed. Items already open in `DECISIONS.md` are listed separately with their locations, not re-flagged as findings.

---

# Part 1: Home and hydronic overview

## The through-line

The 19 August homepage rebuild was good and it landed cleanly. The problem is that **it only landed on the homepage.** Three separate decisions were applied to `index.html` and never propagated to `hydronic/index.html`, so the two pages now argue with each other about batteries, about how the product is described, and about whether the intelligence "learns".

A visitor lands on home, reads a generous framing of their battery, clicks through to hydronic, and finds a comparison table telling them their battery is a fire risk. That is one scroll and one click apart.

Second theme: **two rules in the standing list are broken on the homepage specifically because of the 19 August rebuild.** Ordinal language was deliberately stripped sitewide on 13 August and the rebuild put it back. That is worth knowing before the next rebuild does the same thing again.

---

## Findings

### 1. The battery posture contradicts itself across the two pages

Highest-priority finding. The homepage was rewritten on 19 August to the "wrong tool, not the enemy" framing, per the standing rule. The hydronic comparison table was not.

**`hydronic/index.html:117-119`**
Current: `Fire risk` / `Yes` / `None`
Proposed: Delete the row entirely.

This is an absolute safety claim about a named competitor category, it needs sourcing, and it is precisely the adversarial posture the standing rule bans. It also contradicts `index.html:146`, which now says only "No lithium" and lets the reader draw their own conclusion.

**`hydronic/index.html:112-113`**
Current: `Degradation` / `Fades within ~10 years`
Proposed: `Capacity over time` / `Loses capacity as it ages`

Same softening already applied on the homepage. Drops the specific timeframe, which is the part that invites a complaint.

**`hydronic/index.html:277`**
Current: "Thermal Dawn stores heat and cold directly, so your dawn solar becomes evening comfort without the conversion losses, degradation, or fire risk. It's infrastructure that lasts decades, not a battery that fades in 10 years."
Proposed: "Thermal Dawn stores heat and cold directly, so your dawn solar becomes evening comfort without the conversion losses. It's infrastructure built to last decades."

**Note the page also contradicts itself.** `hydronic/index.html:293-294` ("I already have a battery. Does this still help?") is the best statement of the correct posture anywhere on the site, and it sits forty lines below a table calling batteries a fire risk. Keep 293-294 exactly as written.

---

### 2. The homepage hero still carries the frame the homepage body abandoned

**`index.html:34`** and the meta description
Current: "Australian-made thermal storage that replaces your gas boiler and runs your heating, cooling, and hot water on solar you've already generated, for around half the cost of a home battery."
Proposed: "Australian-made thermal storage that replaces your gas boiler and runs your heating, cooling and hot water on solar you've already generated. One system instead of two."

The comment at `index.html:166` states the section below was deliberately "reframed from 'half the cost of a battery' to 'one system instead of two'". The hero was not updated, so the page makes the old argument at the top and the new one 130 lines later. This is an incomplete edit rather than the open D1 decision: whichever way D1 lands, these two blocks should agree with each other.

**`hydronic/index.html:281`**
Current: "Our target is around half the cost of a comparable lithium battery system for heating, cooling, and hot water, with no degradation and no replacement costs in 10 years."
Proposed: "Total installed cost depends on your home size, existing pipework and electrical setup. Book a free, no-obligation site assessment for a fixed quote."

Three problems in one sentence: the retired frame, an absolute ("no degradation"), and a ten-year figure sitting next to our own cost claim in a section about what we charge.

---

### 3. "No counting installs" is broken on the homepage, and it is a regression

The 13 August changelog records "Ordinal language removed sitewide". The 19 August rebuild reintroduced it.

**`index.html:146`**
Current: "Across our first two homes, the heat pump stayed off through the entire 5pm to 9pm peak on 59 of the last 63 evenings."
Proposed: "Across our Victorian homes, the heat pump stayed off through the entire 5pm to 9pm peak on 59 of the last 63 evenings."

**`index.html:366`**
Current: "Come and see the hardware, and ask us anything. Our first install is a few streets away."
Proposed: "Come and see the hardware, and ask us anything. One of our Melbourne installs is a few streets away."

**`hydronic/index.html:253`**
Current: "...Across both homes, on 59 of the last 63 evenings, the heat pump hasn't run at all between 5pm and 9pm."
Proposed: "...On 59 of the last 63 evenings, the heat pump hasn't run at all between 5pm and 9pm."

The count adds nothing to the claim and the sample size is already carried by "63 evenings".

---

### 4. The lazy-case-study paragraph was rewritten on home and left standing on hydronic

**`hydronic/index.html:253`** (the whole block)
Current: "Different homes, same system. Hawthorn is a radiator home and a deliberately complicated retrofit, the kind that teaches you the most. A Gippsland home on a concrete slab went in and out in two days and hasn't hiccuped since. That matters more than it sounds: one radiator home, one slab home, running the same hardware and the same software, configured per house..."

Proposed: replace with the homepage's rebuilt version, `index.html:266-269`:

> **How it runs.** It charges when power is cheapest, whether that's a free window, your own solar, or late-night off-peak. Then it holds the heat and runs your house through the evening with the compressor off.
>
> Radiators or a concrete slab, it's the same hardware and the same software. You set your tariff and the temperature you want. It handles the rest.

The homepage version is roughly half the words and answers "will it work in my house" rather than narrating what happened to us. "The kind that teaches you the most" is a benefit to Thermal Dawn, not to the reader.

---

### 5. "Our AI optimises" and "the system learns your home" overstate shipped behaviour

**`hydronic/index.html:191-192`**
Current: "The system learns your home" / "Our AI optimises charging times based on your solar forecast, local weather, and your tariff schedule, so you're always comfortable and always on the cheapest possible energy."
Proposed: "It schedules around your tariff" / "The controls plan charging around your electricity prices, your solar forecast and the weather, so you're comfortable and running on the cheapest energy available that day."

Two issues. "Learns" is an adaptive-behaviour claim, and per the 17 August ruling it should not be used unless that behaviour is live in the shipped controls. "Always on the cheapest possible energy" is an absolute that a tariff edge case will eventually break. The homepage already uses the defensible version at `index.html:268`. See also finding 11.

---

### 6. "For free" is true in one of the three charging modes the same page describes

**`hydronic/index.html:34`**
Current: "...delivering it through your existing radiators and underfloor heating, all evening, for free."
Proposed: "...delivering it through your existing radiators and underfloor heating, all evening."

**`hydronic/index.html:184`**
Current: "Heat your home for free at night"
Proposed: "Heat your home on stored energy at night"

`hydronic/index.html:143` correctly says the store charges on off-peak and that "you're still buying your heat at the cheapest rate on your tariff instead of the dearest". That is the honest version, and it is directly contradicted by "for free" twice above it. The free-midday-window case at `:147` is the only one where free is literally true.

---

### 7. Warranty durations appear on the pre-order pages

Outside the pages briefed, but the standing rule says "no warranty duration is stated anywhere", so flagging locations rather than proposing copy:

- `pre-order/index.html:67` "Extended warranty: +2 years beyond standard cover"
- `pre-order/index.html:90` "Warranty Standard Standard +2 years"
- `pre-order/founder-premium/index.html:60` "Extended warranty: +2 years beyond standard"
- `thank-you/founder-premium/index.html:30` "the extended warranty"
- `pre-order/terms/index.html:40` references "extended warranty" (**legal copy, flag only, do not reword**)

"+2 years beyond standard" is a relative duration attached to an undefined standard, which is arguably worse than naming a number: it promises a comparison the customer cannot make. `hydronic/index.html:298` uses the approved wording ("comprehensive warranty coverage") and is fine.

---

### 8. Fleet figures on the homepage do not match the audited canonicals

**`index.html:259-261`**
Current: `Saved $2,399` / `Gas never burned 49,207 MJ` / `CO₂ avoided 2,524 kg`

`DECISIONS.md` records the baked fallbacks as the 17 August audited canonicals: fleet $2,260 / 47,311 MJ / 2,426 kg. The source comment at `index.html:242` says these are "Nick's current readings, newer than the 17 Aug audit doc".

Both cannot be true. Either these are fallbacks, in which case they should match the audit, or they are live readings, in which case they should not be baked into the HTML at all.

**No replacement proposed.** Per the brief, measured figures get queried, not substituted. What needs checking is whether the Warragul box has actually taken the corrected config from `dd5a285`, because the pre-fix feed was over-crediting by $43.62 and rising about $1.30 a day. The gas figure is internally consistent with the daily rates; the dollar figure is the one to verify.

---

### 9. En-dash ranges, which the mechanical check does not catch

INDEX reports zero em dashes, correctly. It does not test en dashes, and house style writes ranges as "to".

- `hydronic/index.html:69` "3–5 years" → "3 to 5 years"
- `hydronic/index.html:74` "3–4 bedroom" → "3 to 4 bedroom"
- `hydronic/index.html:285` "3–5 years" → "3 to 5 years"

Also present on `hydronic/pricing/index.html:233` and elsewhere. Worth adding an en-dash counter to `copy:dump` so this stops needing a human.

---

### 10. Minor: jargon and consistency

**`hydronic/index.html:298`**
Current: "smart controls + app, remote monitoring & OTA updates (opt-in)"
Proposed: "smart controls and app, remote monitoring and software updates (opt-in)"

"OTA" is trade language. "Remote software updates" is the customer phrasing, per the 17 August ruling, and the ampersands are inconsistent with the rest of the page.

## What is working, and should not be touched

**`hydronic/index.html:138-158`, "Works with Your Solar. Works Without It Too."** The strongest section on either page. It kills the biggest disqualifier a reader can bring, does it in four short cases, and the free-midday-window paragraph is genuinely current on where retail tariffs are heading. Do not shorten this.

**`hydronic/index.html:293-294`**, the "I already have a battery" FAQ. The clearest statement of the correct battery posture anywhere on the site. If the comparison table above it gets rewritten, rewrite it towards this.

**`index.html:143-146`**, the battery reframe. Lands the argument without picking a fight.

**Origin scoping** is disciplined throughout. `index.html:337` explicitly says the heat pump is sourced rather than built, which is exactly the rule and is rarer than it should be in this kind of copy.

**The peak window** reads 5pm to 9pm consistently across all three pages. No 3pm or 4pm variants found anywhere.

---

## One thing worth deciding soon, not a finding

The homepage stat is "59 of the last 63 evenings", measured to mid-August. A fuller winter figure now exists in the claims register (row 1b), covering the whole season on a larger sample. It is a stronger number on every axis: bigger sample, harder test, and a timeframe a reader feels.

The site will also quietly go stale as it stands, since "the last 63 evenings" ages without anyone noticing. Either wire the stat to the same query that produces it, or diarise a refresh. The first is a small job and removes the problem permanently.

# Part 2: How It Works

**Added 21 August 2026.** Covers `hydronic/how-it-works/index.html` and the embedded interactive at `assets/animations/hydronic-before-after.html`, reviewed against the rendered HTML rather than the copy dump alone.

## The through-line

This is the best-written page on the site. The site-assessment, will-it-fit and what-to-expect sections are specific, honest and answer the questions a real buyer asks, including several most companies dodge. The 450mm depth, the two tank shapes, the gas-line capping, the lead time, "we're happy to be your first call, but you're never dependent on us being the only one". That is genuinely good work and none of it should be touched.

Two problems sit on top of it.

**The page makes the "learns" claim four times, and its own embedded diagram already has the correct wording.** The interactive says "Schedules around your tariff". The prose says "Our AI learns", "It Learns. It Optimises.", "builds an increasingly accurate model", "the system learns your home". The fix is fifty pixels away from the problem.

**It is the third different battery posture on the site.** Home says wrong tool. Hydronic says fire risk. This page says "Something Better".

---

## Findings

### 11. "It Learns. It Optimises." is the page's headline claim and it overstates shipped behaviour

Four instances, all breaking the 17 August ruling that adaptive behaviour is not claimed unless it is live in the shipped controls.

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:223`** (h2)
Current: "It Learns. It Optimises. It Just Works."
Proposed: "It Plans Ahead. It Just Works."

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:111`**
Current: "Our AI learns Australian weather patterns, energy tariffs, and your home's thermal rhythms, optimising performance automatically."
Proposed: "The controls plan each day around Australian weather, your tariff and how your home holds heat, automatically."

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:225`**
Current: "Over time it builds an increasingly accurate model of your specific home, how quickly it heats up, how well it retains heat overnight, how demand changes with the seasons. Every decision gets better the longer the system runs."
Proposed: "It works from your home's own behaviour: how quickly it heats up, how well it holds heat overnight, how demand shifts with the seasons. Improvements reach every system by remote software update, so it gets better over time whether or not you do anything."

That last replacement keeps the "gets better" promise, which is worth keeping, but grounds it in something true today (fleet-wide software updates) rather than per-home machine learning.

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:244`**
Current: "First winter: the system learns your home and gets more efficient as it goes."
Proposed: "First winter: we tune the system to your home over the first months and it gets more efficient as it settles in."

**The wording to copy from is already on the page.** `assets/animations/hydronic-before-after.html:125` labels Smart Controls "Schedules around your tariff", and `:126` describes them as "reading the forecast, your tariff windows and how much heat the house has left, then charging on solar or on the cheapest hours overnight. It runs itself." That is accurate, concrete and more persuasive than "AI".

---

### 12. 35 kWh is stated as a single capacity, but the page sells two tank sizes

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:163`**
Current: "35kWh — Thermal storage capacity, enough for a full evening and overnight in most Australian homes"

Eighty lines later, `:211-212` offers a 250L cylindrical store and a 500L rectangular one. A reader who picks the smaller tank has just been told they get 35 kWh, and a 250L store cannot hold what a 500L store holds.

Proposed: "35kWh — Thermal storage capacity in our 500L store, enough for a full evening and overnight in most Australian homes. The 250L store holds less; which one suits comes out of your heat load."

Or state both figures. Either is fine, one figure for two products is not.

**This is baked in several places**, so it is a sweep rather than a line edit:
- `assets/animations/hydronic-before-after.html:123` "35 kWh of stored heat"
- `assets/animations/day-night-storage-animation.html:340`, `:379`, `:401`, `:412`
- `assets/animations/gas-replacement-interactive.html:263`, `:271`
- `assets/animations/heating-comparison-table.html:74`, `:92`, `:110` "35kWh Australian-made thermal storage tank"

**Do not substitute a number.** Per the brief, if 35 kWh is a measured or rated figure it should be checked against the actual store spec before anything moves, and the Warragul dashboard reports total storage differently again (tank plus slab). Worth one query that settles it everywhere.

---

### 13. Third battery posture, and another absolute safety claim

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:158`** (h2)
Current: "Not a Battery. Something Better for Heating."
Proposed: "Not a Battery. Built for a Different Job."

"Something better" is a superiority claim about the whole category. "Different job" is the standing rule's framing and is what the section actually goes on to argue.

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:160`**
Current: "It holds a large amount of energy in a compact volume, releases it at a consistent temperature, and doesn't degrade with use. No charge-cycle limit, no capacity loss over time, no fire risk. The same tank that stores your solar energy today will still be doing exactly the same job long after a battery would have been replaced."
Proposed: "It holds a large amount of energy in a compact volume and releases it at a consistent temperature. No charge-cycle limit and no lithium. The same tank that stores your solar energy today will still be doing exactly the same job in fifteen years."

Removes the third "no fire risk" instance, the "no capacity loss over time" absolute, and the comparative jab in the closing clause.

**Credit where due:** the interactive handles this correctly. `hydronic-before-after.html:130` reads "A battery works alongside the thermal store rather than against it: battery for appliances, thermal store for heating, cooling and hot water. It also means a smaller battery goes further." That is the best sentence on the subject anywhere on the site.

---

### 14. The interactive assumes the reader owns solar and a battery

**`assets/animations/hydronic-before-after.html:67`**
Current: "You have solar and a battery, but your heating still burns gas. None of that clean energy is reaching your biggest load."
Proposed: "Your heating still burns gas, and it is the biggest energy load in the house. Any clean energy you generate goes everywhere except there."

**`assets/animations/hydronic-before-after.html:113`** (Solar Panels detail, gas state)
Current: "Your panels generate clean energy all day, and none of it reaches your heating."
Proposed: keep as is, it is conditional on the reader having clicked the solar node.

The opening line is the problem because it is the default state: the first thing every visitor reads. `hydronic/index.html:138-158` is an entire section arguing that the product works without solar, and this diagram opens by telling a reader without solar that the diagram is not about them.

The visual treatment is right, incidentally. Greying out Solar Panels and Home Battery with a cross, captioned "Generating, but not heating" and "Stores electricity, not heat", makes the wrong-tool argument without a word of prose. Keep that.

---

### 15. "Without touching the grid" is contradicted by the page's own timeline

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:146`**
Current: "Stored thermal energy circulates through your radiators and underfloor circuits, keeping every room at your set temperature without touching the grid. Your home stays comfortable. Your meter barely moves."
Proposed: "Stored thermal energy circulates through your radiators and underfloor circuits, keeping every room at your set temperature while the heat pump stays off. Your home stays comfortable and your meter barely moves."

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:102`**
Current: "The only difference is the energy powering them cost you almost nothing."
Proposed: "The only difference is when you paid for the energy, and how little it cost."

Twenty lines above, `:125` says the system "starts pre-charging from off-peak grid power, the cheapest available energy". So it does touch the grid, deliberately, and the page says so. The honest claim is that the heat pump is off during peak, which is exactly what the measured evidence supports. "Without touching the grid" claims something stronger than the data and weaker than the truth, because grid-at-off-peak is the smarter story.

---

### 16. "R290 reaches 70°C" reads as a measurement, not a spec

**`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:192`**
Current: "R290 reaches 70°C. That matches what most gas boilers actually run at, so your existing radiators work as they are, no resizing."
Proposed: "R290 is specified to 70°C. That matches what most gas boilers actually run at, so your existing radiators work as they are, no resizing."

DECISIONS settled 19 August that 70°C is a spec commitment, not a measurement, and that spec and measurement must stay distinguishable. `:164` gets this right with "Up to 70°C". `:192` and `:284` state it flat. Measured peak is 65.0°C, so the distinction matters if anyone ever checks.

Same fix at **`:284`**: "Our R290 configuration runs at up to 70°C" is fine as written. Leave it.

---

### 17. Seven FAQs and no FAQPage schema

`hydronic/how-it-works/index.html:265-292` is a properly built FAQ block with seven question-and-answer pairs, and there is no `application/ld+json` anywhere on the page. Nor on `index.html` or `hydronic/index.html`.

This is a page whose entire job is answering the questions people type into Google, and it is passing up rich results on every one of them. Not copy, but it is the highest-leverage SEO item on the page and it costs a block of JSON.

---

### 18. Live bug: wrong domain on a CTA

**`assets/animations/heating-tool.html:938`**
Current: `'https://www.thermaldawn.com/register'`

Every other URL in the codebase uses `thermaldawn.com.au`, 85 instances against this one. If `.com` does not resolve or redirect, this is a dead CTA inside an interactive tool. Worth checking rather than assuming, since the domain may be held and redirected, but it should not be inconsistent either way.

---

## What is working, and should not be touched

**`:186-215`, the site assessment and will-it-fit sections.** The strongest commercial writing on the site. Naming the outdoor unit at 450mm deep, giving both tank dimensions, telling people to send a photo before anyone visits, and admitting height is usually the real constraint. This is what removes friction from a hydronic retrofit conversation and almost nobody in this category does it.

**`:243`, the gas line.** "A qualified, licensed plumber caps the gas line, arranged through us or by your own tradesperson. Disconnecting the gas meter to cut the daily supply charge entirely is optional, we'll walk you through whether it's worth it for you." Honest, specific, and it defuses the single scariest part of the job.

**`:288`, the servicing answer.** "No proprietary lock-in, no special parts to order from us, and no service contract you're tied into. We're happy to be your first call, but you're never dependent on us being the only one." This is the answer to the real objection about buying hardware from a young company, and it is answered without defensiveness.

**`:178`, the radiator cooling note.** Volunteering that hydronic cooling does not work through radiators, and why, before anyone asks. That is the evidence-first posture doing its job.

**`:139`, "Any remaining solar goes to your hot water or back to the grid."** A small honest detail that makes the rest more believable.

**The interactive's component detail copy** at `hydronic-before-after.html:104-138` is uniformly better than the page prose it sits inside. If any section needs rewriting, that copy is the house voice at its best and worth using as the reference.

---

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | "Learns / AI" claim, four instances, fix already on the page | High, breaks a standing ruling |
| 12 | 35 kWh single figure, two tank sizes, baked in 9 places | High, needs a query first |
| 13 | Third battery posture plus a third "no fire risk" | High, breaks a standing rule |
| 14 | Interactive assumes solar and a battery | Medium, contradicts a whole section |
| 15 | "Without touching the grid" vs own timeline | Medium, self-contradiction |
| 16 | "R290 reaches 70°C" spec vs measurement | Low, but it is a settled decision |
| 17 | No FAQPage schema on seven FAQs | Low for copy, high for SEO |
| 18 | `.com` instead of `.com.au` on a CTA | Bug, verify then fix |
